title: Air Ticket Fare Brands: Name-Correction Charges Standing on a Cancelled Booking
content:
# Air Ticket Fare Brands: Name-Correction Charges Standing on a Cancelled Booking

Under Air Ticket Fare Brands the desk determines what a name correction on the cancelled booking adds to the value released from two things: whether a name-correction line stands on that booking, and whether the fare brand that produced the voucher makes credits transferable. What a name correction settles is an amount in dollars added to the value released.

What the name-correction lines were charged is the total of the change-fee lines standing on the cancelled booking for the reason of a name correction.

| A name-correction line on the cancelled booking | Credits under the brand that produced the voucher | What is added to the value released |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stands | non-transferable | a share of 1.0 of what those lines were charged, the whole of it |
| stands | transferable | a share of 0.5 of what those lines were charged, half of it |
| none stands | either way | nothing is added to the value released for a name correction |

Worked on hypothetical figures: name-correction change-fee lines of 75.00 and 45.00 stand on the cancelled booking, so what those lines were charged comes to 120.00. Where the brand that produced the voucher makes credits non-transferable, the whole of that amount, 120.00, is added to the value released. Where that brand makes credits transferable, half of it, 60.00, is added to the value released. Where no name-correction line stands on the cancelled booking, nothing is added to the value released for a name correction, whichever way the brand treats the transfer of credits.
